justification: Both surfaces include carved human forms and small circular/disc-like symbols, but A is dominated by dense horizontal rows of hieroglyphic script with two subordinate kneeling figures at the base, while B is a single freestanding humanoid statue bearing a few incised marks on its torso. The overall composition, density of sign-work, and relationship between figure and inscription differ fundamentally, so the correspondence is limited to generic motifs rather than a shared iconographic scheme.
